images.title: Parallel line, third angle
images.purpose: Show how a line through the top vertex parallel to the base turns the two base angles into angles at A that fill a straight angle.
images.composition: One triangle in the lower centre with a long straight line through its top vertex above the base; all marks near A and the base ends.
exact_structure: Triangle ABC with base BC horizontal at the bottom, B at the left, C at the right, A above; angle at B is 50° and angle at C is 70°.
A long dark horizontal line XY through A, parallel to BC, X at its left end and Y at its right end.
At B a teal (#0072B2) arc labelled 50°; at A, between AX and AB, a matching teal arc labelled 50°.
At C an amber (#E69F00) arc labelled 70°; at A, between AC and AY, a matching amber arc labelled 70°.
At A between AB and AC a reddish purple (#CC79A7) arc labelled 60°.
The three angles at A (50°, 60°, 70°) together fill the straight line XY.
rejection: the angles at A not matching the base angles (50° and 70°)
an angle other than 60° between AB and AC
images.takeaway: The three angles at A fill a straight angle of 180°, so the third angle is 180° − 50° − 70° = 60°.
images.description: Triangle ABC with a line XY through A parallel to BC and angles 50°, 60° and 70° at A.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Look first at the equal coloured pairs, then at the purple angle left over.

image_decisions.why: The parallel line is the key picture for finding the third angle.
